title: Toward C:open-ended, mixed: a kind-specific waste keeps 2-3 trait branches coexisting in the fed vortices and the dominant class keeps changing to classes never dominant before through T=12000 (6 and 9 first-time dominants after t=3000, vs 1 and 1 in the kind-blind twin), but the novelty curve decelerates (10-12 classes by t~4000, +3 in the next 8000 t), the branches wander back, and the selection is not visible per birth or per fusion
summary: world.py: the continuous-trait fed vortices (20261027T1230-c58-vortex-trait-climb: label density c and trait mass z copied linearly where the vortex eats; whole-vortex trait-blind mutation +-0.4 every 50 t) plus a waste W released by eating (pw 0.25, Dw 1, dw 0.002) carrying the eater's trait; gain k(1 + 0.25(1 - W/(1+W) G)), G = exp(-(theta - theta_W)^2/(2 0.4^2)); the kind-blind twin (sw 0, G = 1) has the same ecology and mutation draws and a gain that does not depend on the trait. T=12000, seeds 1-2 (trait.py, novelty.py, curves.py): distinct dominant classes 10/12 vs 2/3; first-time dominants after t=3000 6/9 vs 1/1; classes ever held by >= 3 vortices 15/13 vs 6/5, of which 12/10 already by t=6000 (novelty_curves_long.png); trait branches near +2 and -2.5 at t=12000 on seed 2 (L_s2_spec_maps.png). Fresh seeds 3-4, T=6000: 7/4 vs 2/2 dominant classes, 3/1 vs 1/1 first-time dominants after t=3000, 10/6 vs 4/4 classes held by >= 3. Persistent splits are 2-4x fewer in the kind-specific arm; births per vortex are not higher in rare classes (freqbirth.py), the fused vortex takes the larger parent's trait at 90% of mixed-trait fusions in both arms and the rarer class at 46-51% (fusion.py), so where the frequency dependence acts (probably locally, the waste reaches ~22 px) is not resolved.

finding.operator: kind-specific waste (negative frequency dependence carried by a diffusing, decaying field recording the eater's trait) on a heritable scalar trait
finding.control: kind-blind waste twin (sw 0: same ecology and draws, gain independent of the trait), 4 seeds; T=12000 on seeds 1 2
finding.result: sustained turnover (first-time dominants after t=3000: 6, 9, 3, 1 vs 1, 1, 1, 1) and 2-3 coexisting branches, but the cumulative class count decelerates (12/10 by t=6000, 15/13 by t=12000) and returns to earlier dominant classes dominate the spell sequence (25 and 24 returns in 35-36 spells)

limits: 128^2, one parameter point, no dt/2 or grid test, no labkit pack of this world (its I and D rest on the parent worlds' packs). The waste reads the eater's trait and the gain reads the vortex's trait: the negative frequency dependence is written, so turnover is expected from the rule; the vortices' own heredity carries it (copying and mutation never read the trait; jumps of living vortices away from a mutation 0-3 per run). One scalar trait: a random walk of the branches also reaches new bins, and the long-run increase (+3 classes in 8000 t) is no faster than such wandering; on seed 1 the lower branch reached class -7 and came back to -4. Heredity is weaker than with no waste (daughter class fidelity 75-82% vs 85-89% in the kind-blind twin; within-vortex spread 0.03-0.05 vs 0.01), because diverse traits fuse. Seed 4 shows little turnover (4 dominant classes, 1 first-time dominant after t=3000). Rarity is measured as the global class share; the waste is local, so a local measure may show what the global one does not. Next: a trait vector (20261027T1401-c58-vortex-trait3d) to test whether more trait dimensions stop the deceleration.
